meta.gap: ~+6–8" running vertical to control a ball over a 10-ft rim
meta.drivers: Vertical = max strength × reactive (elastic) power × jump technique × power-to-weight. We build all four.
meta.note: Marathon training likely suppressed your vertical — expect some to return 'for free' as endurance fatigue clears and you train power.

phases.name: Vertical Base
phases.priority: Build the strength base — concurrent with the 70.3, done FRESH
phases.tagline: Foundational max strength + knee-safe plyo, woven into the tri block. Low volume, high quality, fresh legs.
focus: Build max lower-body strength (squat + hinge) — the foundation under every vertical.
Start plyometrics at the BOTTOM of the ladder — tendon prep first (PFPS-safe).
Drill jump technique: approach, penultimate step, arm swing — free inches most people leave on the table.
Ankle/hip mobility + single-leg strength for landing control and force transfer.

sessions.detail: Back squat 4×5 heavy · RDL 3×6 · Bulgarian split squat · calf raises

sessions.title: Low plyo
sessions.detail: Pogo + ankle hops 3×20 — build tendon stiffness

sessions.title: Jump technique + power
sessions.detail: Box jumps (land soft) · broad jumps · approach-step drills · arm-swing timing

sessions.title: Ankle/hip mobility
sessions.detail: 5–10 min — plus keep the knee staples (step-downs)

nutrition.mindset: Fuel the strength work — maintenance/slow recomp, high protein. No cut yet (that's Phase B).

phases.notes: These slot into the /tri week (Mon power, Fri plyo). Progress plyo only when the knee is quiet — quality over quantity, land soft, full recovery between reps.

phases.name: Dunk Peak + Cut
phases.priority: Peak the vertical + win the bet by Dec 31
phases.tagline: Endurance drops to maintenance — full explosive focus. Reactive plyo, jump-specific practice, CNS freshness, and the cut for power-to-weight.
focus: Reactive/elastic plyo (depth jumps, bounds) — ONLY once the knee is bulletproof.
Jump-specific practice: approach dunk attempts, rim touches, ball control.
Maintain heavy max strength at low volume — keep the force base sharp.
Cut ~0.5 lb/wk — every pound lost is essentially free vertical.

sessions.title: Reactive plyo
sessions.detail: Depth jumps · bounds · approach jumps (knee-ready) + jump technique

sessions.title: Power
sessions.detail: Trap-bar jumps · single-leg power · loaded jumps

sessions.title: Court practice
sessions.detail: Approach dunk attempts · rim touches · ball control

nutrition.mindset: The ONLY hard-cut window in the whole plan. ~0.5 lb/wk, no faster. High protein to hold power. This lean-out also reveals the abs.

phases.notes: Palming is a separate skill — a slightly under-inflated ball or a two-hand dunk counts. Clarify with your friend what wins the bet.

progression: 1 · Foundation (low intensity): pogo hops, ankle hops, line hops, rope skipping — build tendon stiffness first.
2 · Eccentric control: slow step-downs (already doing) + low box step-offs, stick the landing — learn to absorb force.
3 · Bilateral jumps: countermovement jumps, box jumps (jump UP = soft landing), broad jumps.
4 · Unilateral: single-leg box jumps, short bounds.
5 · Reactive (HIGH intensity — knee must be bulletproof first): depth jumps, repeated hops, approach jumps.
Rule: advance a stage only when fully pain-free. Low volume, high intent, land soft, full recovery. Knee talks → drop back a stage.
technique: One-foot vs two-foot: test both. Most leapers jump higher off ONE foot with a running approach (more elastic); some are two-foot dominant.
Penultimate step: a long, low second-to-last step converts horizontal speed into vertical lift — the biggest technique lever.
Arm swing: a big double-arm (two-foot) or hard opposite-arm drive (one-foot) adds real inches. Time it with the jump.
Approach: 3–5 controlled, accelerating steps. Practice the rhythm, not just max effort.
Practice the full movement — approach + jump + reach — not just standing jumps.
testing: Standing reach: flat-footed, one arm fully up against a wall — mark it.
Max touch: jump and mark the highest point you touch (test both one- and two-foot).
Vertical = max touch − standing reach. Track monthly.
Targets: rim = 120". To control a ball over it, aim to touch ~126" (rim + ~6" clearance).
Re-test the 1st of each month — watch the gap to 126" shrink.

guide.vertical: Your vertical is built from four things: raw max strength (heavy squats), reactive/elastic power (plyometrics — how fast you apply that strength), jump technique (approach + arm swing), and power-to-weight (getting lean). Phase A builds strength + technique + tendon base; Phase B peaks the reactive power and cuts the weight. Both matter — most people only train one.
guide.ballcontrol: Getting your hand high enough is half the battle; controlling the ball over the rim is the other half. Palming a full basketball depends on hand size — if you can't, use a slightly under-inflated ball, a smaller ball, or a two-hand dunk. Decide with your friend what counts for the bet, and practice the actual finish, not just rim touches.
guide.knee: This is the goal where your PFPS history matters most — plyometrics are the exact eccentric-impact load that flared the knee. Follow the progression ladder strictly, keep the eccentric step-downs in as insurance, and never skip stages. If the knee objects, plyo comes out before anything else. A dunk isn't worth re-breaking the knee that's carrying every other goal.
guide.nutrition: Get lean in Phase B (Nov–Dec) — a gentle ~0.5 lb/wk cut. Power-to-weight is one of the fastest ways to add relative vertical, and the same lean-out reveals the abs (goal #3). Keep protein high (~1 g/lb) so you hold the muscle and power while the fat comes off.

gym.note: Phase A (base): 2× full split — heavy strength + skills. Phase B (peak): 3–4× power-focused — max strength, reactive plyo, and a power day, plus one short upper maintenance session.
